justification.text: The quotient is the problem's probability that x precedes y in a uniformly random linear extension: the denominator total_ext.ncard is the number of linear extensions, which is positive because total_ext is a finite set (maps from the finite P into Icc 1 (card P)) and every finite poset has a linear extension; and were it 0 the quotient would be 0 ∉ Icc (1/3) (2/3), so Lean's x/0 = 0 could only make the claim false, never vacuously true.

acknowledged_hazards.location: ↑{σ | σ ∈ total_ext ∧ σ x < σ y}.ncard / ↑total_ext.ncard

justification.text: `Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)` is the docstring's own encoding: linear extensions are 'order preserving bijections of P onto 1, ..., n', with n = |P|. An order map from P onto exactly {1, ..., n} is such a bijection, so both endpoints belong in the range.

theorem Opn.conjecture_1_3_to_2_3 :
    ∀ (P : Type) [Finite P] [PartialOrder P]
    (not_total : ¬ Std.Total (α := P) (· ≤ ·)) (total_ext : Set <| OrderHom P ℕ)
    (total_ext_def : ∀ σ, σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range σ = Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)),
    ∃ x y : P, ({σ ∈ total_ext | σ x < σ y}.ncard / total_ext.ncard : ℚ)
      ∈ Set.Icc (1/3) (2/3) := by
  sorry

witness.text:
/-! Non-vacuity witness (D-4 step 7): Bool × Bool under the product order is a finite poset that is not total ((true, false) and (false, true) are incomparable), and total_ext is defined as exactly the set the membership condition describes. -/

theorem witness : ∃ (P : Type) (inst : PartialOrder P) (total_ext : Set (P →o ℕ)),
  Finite P ∧
    (¬Std.Total fun (x1 x2 : P) => x1 ≤ x2) ∧
      ∀ (σ : P →o ℕ), σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range (⇑σ : P → ℕ) = Set.Icc (1 : ℕ) (Nat.card P) :=
  ⟨Bool × Bool, inferInstance, {σ | Set.range (⇑σ : Bool × Bool → ℕ) = Set.Icc (1 : ℕ) (Nat.card (Bool × Bool))},
    inferInstance,
    fun h => by
      have := h.total (true, false) (false, true)
      simp [Prod.le_def, Bool.le_iff_imp] at this,
    fun σ => Iff.rfl⟩
